method.stack: docker compose -p w3oracle up -d in crates/egret-workflow/oracle-exec (Docker socket mounted into the Kestra container, runs as root); basic auth admin@kestra.io; tenant main; namespace w5a
method.run: POST /api/v1/main/executions/w5a/<id> (multipart, no inputs); poll GET /executions/<id> until terminal
method.outputs: POST /api/v1/main/executions/<id>/actions/eval with body `{{ outputs | toJson }}` (the execution JSON carries no outputs)
method.image_used: `docker events --filter type=container --filter type=image` for the whole session; container create events carry the image as the runner passed it
method.schema: GET /api/v1/plugins/<FQCN> and GET /api/v1/plugins/schemas/flow; cross-checked against Jackson's `N known properties` list from POST /api/v1/main/flows/validate
method.postgres: never touched (no docker exec into the artifact's postgres)

how_to_read_for_egret: raw_records and findings are EVIDENCE of what Kestra did. egret_expected holds typed values Task 2's tests deserialize: `basis` says whether a value was measured, code-derived, or egret-chosen (a deliberate difference from spec §2).

findings.finding: With no containerImage, shell.Commands and shell.Script created their container from `ubuntu` and python.Commands and python.Script from `python:3.13-slim` (docker `create` events, attribute image). The schema defaults agree: shell `"default": "ubuntu"`, python `"default": "python:3.13-slim"`. In the container /etc/os-release read `PRETTY_NAME="Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS"` (shell) and `PRETTY_NAME="Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie)"` with `3.13.15 (main, Sep 19 2026, 01:05:27) [GCC 14.2.0]` (python).

The default runner is Docker: every default-runner run logged `Starting command with container id <id>`, and its outputs carry `"taskRunner": {"containerId": "<64 hex>"}`. The schema's `taskRunner` is `$required: true` with no default in JSON; the default instance is in code: AbstractExecScript.java:52-58 `Docker.builder().type(Docker.class.getName()).pullPolicy(Property.ofValue(PullPolicy.IF_NOT_PRESENT))`. `ubuntu:latest` was pulled once (`Image pulled [ubuntu:latest]`, first run) and not on the 16 later ubuntu runs: consistent with IF_NOT_PRESENT.
findings.basis: measured (runner type); code + consistent observation (pull policy)

findings.finding: GET /api/v1/main/executions/{id} returns task runs with NO `outputs` key on this artifact (raw-first-pass). Outputs were read with POST /api/v1/main/executions/{id}/actions/eval, body `{{ outputs | toJson }}` (`| json` answers `Filter [json] does not exist`).

Successful Docker run outputs: `{"vars": {...}, "exitCode": 0, "taskRunner": {"containerId": ...}, "outputFiles": {...}}`. A failed run still records outputs, without `taskRunner`: `{"vars": {}, "exitCode": 3, "outputFiles": {}}`. Process runner: no `taskRunner` key. `vars` is filled from a stdout line `::{"outputs":{"probe":42}}::` -> `"vars": {"probe": 42}`.

outputFiles [out.txt] -> `"outputFiles": {"out.txt": "kestra:///w5a/q2-output-files-exact/executions/<eid>/tasks/t/<taskRunId>/<random>-out.txt"}`: key = the declared relative path, value = an internal-storage URI (flow id with `_` turned into `-`). `{{ outputFiles['out.txt'] }}` rendered to `<workingDir>/out.txt` (`path_tpl=/tmp/kestra-wd/tmp/5cLNEyvy4c1HIk8EUoa1G8/out.txt`). egret keeps the keys and puts the inline contents in the value (spec §2 row, W9 owns storage).

outputFiles ['*.csv'] with a.csv, b.csv, sub/c.csv and x.txt in the working dir captured exactly `a.csv` and `b.csv` (`Captured 2 output file(s).`): `*` does not descend into sub-directories and keys are paths relative to the working dir.
A declared outputFiles entry that the script never writes is not an error: `"outputFiles": {}`, state SUCCESS, `Captured 0 output file(s).`

inputFiles {in.txt: hello-input, sub/nested.txt: "nested {{ flow.id }}"} landed at `./in.txt` and `./sub/nested.txt` relative to the working dir (sub-directories created), contents rendered (`nested q2_input_files_inline`). The working dir is the same path three ways: `wd_tpl=` ({{ workingDir }}), `PWD=` and `WORKING_DIR=` all `/tmp/kestra-wd/tmp/36A815VjLo5yvGNvJqO8q3`.

warningOnStdErr true, false and unset all ended SUCCESS with `echo to-stderr >&2` then exit 0; python.Script with warningOnStdErr: true and a stderr line also SUCCESS. The stderr line is logged at level ERROR in every case (as W11 measured). The Java field reads `@Schema(title = "Not used anymore, will be removed soon") @Deprecated protected Property<Boolean> warningOnStdErr` (AbstractExecScript.java). CONTRADICTS spec §3 ('sets the task state to WARNING'): the spec is amended to 'accepted, no effect'.

failFast true (and unset: default true) prepends `set -e` to the script: `[/bin/sh -c set -e
false
echo second-ran]` -> FAILED, exitCode 1, `second-ran` not printed. failFast false omits it: `[/bin/sh -c false
echo second-ran]` -> SUCCESS, exitCode 0, `second-ran` printed. The commands are ONE script joined with `
`, so an `exit 3` ends it whatever failFast says (q4_fail_fast_*: all FAILED, exitCode 3). With failFast false the last command decides: `exit 7` last -> FAILED, exitCode 7. A failure logs ERROR `Command failed with exit code <n>`.

(failFast default = true) beforeCommands [echo before-1, false] + commands [echo main] ran as `/bin/sh -c echo '##kestra:log:debug##'
set -e
echo before-1
false
echo '##kestra:log:info##'
echo main`: one script, `set -e` once before the beforeCommands, and beforeCommands' output logged at DEBUG (`DEBUG before-1`) through Kestra's `##kestra:log:<level>##` markers. `false` in beforeCommands failed the task (exitCode 1) before `main`.

Fix round 1: the same beforeCommands with failFast: false ran as `/bin/sh -c echo '##kestra:log:debug##'
echo before-1
false
echo '##kestra:log:info##'
echo main` (no `set -e`), printed `main` and ended SUCCESS, exitCode 0. With failFast: true (explicit) it is FAILED, exitCode 1, no `main`. So `set -e` before beforeCommands is conditional on failFast, as AbstractExecScript.java:179-181 says.

Fix round 1: commands [echo '::{"outputs":{"early":1}}::', exit 4] -> FAILED with outputs `{"vars": {"early": 1}, "exitCode": 4, "outputFiles": {}}`: a failed run keeps the vars emitted before the failure.

Fix round 1: containerImage `python@sha256:7c61056e…` (the local python:3.13-slim) -> the container was created with the image exactly as written, no pull event, `Python 3.13.15`, SUCCESS. A registry with a port was not measured (no registry): Docker.java:988-990 treats a colon before the first `/` as the registry port, and :1025 defaults a missing tag to `latest`.

Fix round 1: a missing `commands` / `script` is refused at save (`tasks[t].commands: must not be null`, `tasks[t].script: must not be null`) on all four types. No `taskRunner`, and `taskRunner: null`, validate clean on shell.Commands and python.Script; every default-runner run in this file has none. The schema's `$required: true` on taskRunner is the @NotNull on a field that has a code default.

Of the 15 base-Task properties every script type accepts (besides `timeout`, which W5a implements), egret's Task deserializer (crates/egret-workflow/src/models/task.rs:663-679) reads id, type, description, retry, disabled, runIf, allowFailure, allowWarning; the other seven -- assets, logLevel, logToFile, policyRefs, taskCache, version, workerSelector -- stay in the leaf spec map and nothing reads them. W5a therefore REFUSES those seven on script types (`refused_in_w5a`), and `version` is refused on the Docker runner too. Kestra accepted `version: '1.9.8'` on a task at save (measured).

Fix round 1: Docker `cpu` is a closed object (`one known property: "cpus"`), `memory` too (`6 known properties: "memory", "memorySwap", "memoryReservation", "oomKillDisable", "kernelMemory", "memorySwappiness"`). W5a implements `cpu.cpus` and `memory.memory` and refuses the other five memory sub-properties.

shell.Script inlines the script after `set -e` (`/bin/sh -c set -e\n<script>`). python.Script writes the script to `<workingDir>/<digits>.py` and runs `set -e\nif [ -n "$VIRTUAL_ENV" ]; then "$VIRTUAL_ENV/bin/python" "<path>"; else "python" "<path>"; fi` (python sys.argv[0] = that path). python.Commands runs its commands as shell lines like shell.Commands.

containerImage: python -> the container was created with image `python` (as written) and Docker pulled `python:latest` (log `Image pulled [python:latest]`, docker image pull event id `python:latest`); `python --version` printed `Python 3.14.7`. Code: Docker.java:1025 `var tag = !parsedTagFromImage.tag.isEmpty() ? parsedTagFromImage.tag : "latest"`. Confirms spec §4: the allowlist matches the reference after defaulting the tag to `latest`.

The kept container (delete: false) had Env `["WORKING_DIR=/tmp/kestra-wd/tmp/4D4h8LtfaXimAFBgDedSTC", "PATH=..."]` (no other Kestra variable), WorkingDir = that dir, User "" (image default), NetworkMode bridge, a Docker-random name (`xenodochial_sinoussi`) and labels kestra.io/{execution-id, flow-id, namespace, task-id, taskrun-attempt=0, taskrun-id}. The attempt label is 0-based.

Docker runner delete: false -> SUCCESS; the container stayed in `docker ps -a` as `Exited (0)`, and its anonymous volume (labelled like the container) stayed too; the logs lack `Container deleted`/`Volume deleted`. With the default (true) both were removed (`Container deleted: <id>`, `Volume deleted: <id>`). Both were removed by hand after the measurement.

taskRunner Process runs the commands INSIDE the Kestra server container: `Starting command with pid 382`, HOSTNAME=ffaf3c6023bd (the id of w3oracle-kestra-1), os-release `Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS` (the server image, not ubuntu:latest), `id -u` = 0. This is the reason egret refuses it at save (spec §2).

POST /flows/validate: an unknown task property -> `Unrecognized field "notAProperty" (class io.kestra.plugin.scripts.shell.Commands), not marked as ignorable (30 known properties: ...)`; an unknown Docker runner property -> the same with `(23 known properties: ...)`, which includes the schema-hidden `image`; `io.kestra.plugin.ee.kubernetes.runner.Kubernetes` -> `Invalid type: io.kestra.plugin.ee.kubernetes.runner.Kubernetes` (EE-only). Accepted at save: inputFiles as a `kestra://` string, targetOS: WINDOWS, pullPolicy: SOMETIMES (a dynamic property, not checked at save).

Each type accepts exactly its flow-schema properties (the 30 in Jackson's error for shell.Commands equal the schema's list). Python types add dependencies, dependencyCacheEnabled, packageManager (UV|PIP, default UV), pythonVersion, uvAutoInstallEnabled, uvInstallerSha256, uvInstallerVersion. Per-type lists and the implemented/handled/refused split are in egret_expected.task_types. Fix round 1 cross-checked all four types against Jackson's lists (30, 30, 37, 37 known properties), equal to the schema.

io.kestra.plugin.scripts.runner.docker.D.sub_properties_basis: measured (accepted: Jackson `one known property: "cpus"` / `6 known properties`); egret-chosen split: only the two that map to a Kubernetes limit are implemented

io.kestra.plugin.core.runner.Process.basis: spec §2 (egret-chosen): Process ran inside the Kestra server container as uid 0

io.kestra.plugin.ee.kubernetes.runner.Ku.basis: spec §2/§3 (egret-chosen): EE FQCN, absent from OSS so nothing is measurable; a closed set, every other property or resources path is refused at save

output_files.basis: measured (keys, glob, missing); spec §2 (egret-chosen: inline contents)

before_commands.basis: measured (both failFast values); agrees with AbstractExecScript.java:179-181 mayAddExitOnErrorCommands

cases.basis: measured (create event image as written, ran Python 3.13.15, no pull)
code (Docker.java:988-990 a colon before the first slash is the registry port; :1025 tag defaults to latest); not measured, no registry
egret-chosen: no Docker Hub normalisation in either direction, so `python:*` does not match it

save_validation.kestra_error_template: Unrecognized field "{property}" (class {fqcn}), not marked as ignorable
save_validation.basis: measured: Kestra itself refuses unknown properties at save, so a named refusal is Kestra's behaviour, not only egret's
